name: FormBeacon – Form Health Monitor
author: Nikhil

sections.description:
FormBeacon helps WordPress site owners detect unhealthy form behavior before it becomes a business problem.

It monitors provider-level submission signals exposed by supported form plugins and highlights forms that may require attention.

Supported providers in this version:
* Contact Form 7
* WPForms
* Gravity Forms

FormBeacon stores operational metadata only:
* form provider
* form ID
* event type
* timestamps
* health status

FormBeacon does not store personal submission content such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, message bodies, or uploaded files.

Privacy Policy

FormBeacon stores minimal operational telemetry to monitor form health. This includes the form ID, success/failure status, and aggregated event timestamps. It does not store personal identifiers (PII), request bodies, user IP addresses, uploaded file names, or any form field content.

All telemetry data is stored locally within your WordPress database and is automatically pruned after the retention period configured in FormBeacon Settings.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/formbeacon directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to FormBeacon in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Configure your health thresholds and alert email settings.
sections.faq:
Does FormBeacon guarantee email inbox delivery?

No. FormBeacon monitors submission health signals exposed by supported form plugins. It does not guarantee SMTP delivery, inbox delivery, or third-party CRM delivery.

Does FormBeacon store personal form submission data?

No. FormBeacon is designed to store operational metadata only. No names, emails, phone numbers, message bodies, or file names are ever stored.

Which form plugins are supported?

This version supports Contact Form 7, WPForms, and Gravity Forms.

Does FormBeacon track both successes and failures for all form plugins?

Yes. As of version 1.1.0, FormBeacon tracks both successes and failures for all three supported providers:
* Contact Form 7 — mail sent (success) and mail failed (failure).
* WPForms — process complete (success), AJAX validation error response (failure), and spam detection blocks (failure).
* Gravity Forms — entry saved (success), validation failure via gform_validation (failure), and spam flagged via gform_entry_is_spam (failure).
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Added failure tracking for WPForms: AJAX validation errors (wpforms_ajax_submit_error_response) and spam detection (wpforms_process_spam_entry).
  • Added failure tracking for Gravity Forms: validation failures (gform_validation) and spam detection (gform_entry_is_spam).
  • Added detailed error context (failed field labels, error counts) to failure event logs.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
